findings.issue: Audit-report path convention is inconsistent across the audit wave. Task 8 writes its report to `logs/working/task-8/code-audit-1.json` (a per-task working-review path, JSON), while Task 9 writes `logs/audits/security-audit.md` and Task 10 writes `logs/audits/test-audit.md` (a dedicated audits dir, markdown). All three are members of the same Audit Wave and should use ONE convention. The `logs/working/task-{N}/` tree is conventionally for reviewer reports during task execution, not for the audit-task's own deliverable; Task 8 also diverges from siblings on both directory and format (.json vs .md).
findings.fix: Pick one convention for the Audit Wave deliverables and apply it to Tasks 8/9/10. Recommended: move Task 8's report to `logs/audits/code-audit.md` (aligning dir+format with Tasks 9/10), and update every reference in Task 8 (Acceptance Criteria last item, Verification Steps -> Audit deliverable, Details -> Files, Post-completion decisions.md link) accordingly. If JSON is intentionally preferred for the code audit, at minimum relocate it under `logs/audits/` (e.g. `logs/audits/code-audit.json`) so all three audits share the same directory.

findings.issue: Verification Steps contains only an `### Automated` subsection whose body states tests are not applicable for an audit and instead lists report-existence/completeness checks. This is acceptable content for an audit task, but the check is really a smoke-style deliverable check placed under the `Automated` heading. Tasks 10 correctly uses a `### Smoke` subsection (`test -f ... -> report written`) for the equivalent check.
findings.fix: For consistency with Task 10, move the report-existence/completeness checks under a `### Smoke` subsection (e.g. `test -f work/17-funnel-multi-entry/logs/audits/security-audit.md`). Cosmetic; content is otherwise complete and correct.

findings.issue: Audit tasks (8/9/10) have `reviewers: []` and no `## Reviewers` section. Per the template the `## Reviewers` section is listed as present/non-empty; for self-reviewing audit tasks its absence is expected and correct (the task is itself the review). Recorded as informational only to confirm the intentional omission was reviewed, not a defect.
findings.fix: No action required. Confirmed correct: audit tasks are self-reviewing (`reviewers: []`), so the `## Reviewers` section is legitimately absent. TDD Anchor is also correctly absent on all three audit tasks (read-only, produce reports not code).
